title: Finite-set characterization of the recursive condition
statement: Let $A$, $B$, and $	ext{Kont}$ be predicates on the natural numbers, and let $r,t,c$ be natural numbers. The recursive condition that makes $r$ successive choices between $A$ and $B$, incrementing the counter exactly when $A$ is chosen and ending with $	ext{Kont}$, holds at $(r,t,c)$ if and only if there is a finite set $T\subseteq\{t,t+1,\ldots,t+r-1\}$ such that $A(y)$ holds for every $y\in T$, $B(y)$ holds for every other $y$ in that interval, and $	ext{Kont}(c+|T|)$ holds.
hypotheses_covered: Predicates A, B, and Kont on natural numbers
Natural numbers r, t, and c
